answer: The strongest lever is simple: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because juniper only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, umber is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any forge approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
